text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Dedicated pool error spike detected for customer ArgosCorp (tenant: argos-prod) in us-west-2. 5xx rate > 35% over 5m. Pager assigned to Priya.
Priya: I'm on it, pulling logs and checking pool health.
Priya: Sam @Sam can you confirm if any infra changes were rolled out to us-west-2 in the last hour?
Sam: Noted. I didn't deploy anything. Checking node health in pool-42 (argon-dedicated-usw2).
Elena: saw a blip in KV cache evictions earlier, could be correlation. ETA 10m to fetch profiles.
Priya: Customer impact: ArgosCorp reports increased 504s and degraded token throughput, intermittent latency 2-6s per token. They're on Dedicated pool-42.
Jamal: tagging me—I'm the account lead. I'll open a bridge with their SRE. They have active workflows in production.
Nikki: I've messaged ArgosCorp support channel (internal) to acknowledge. They asked for ETA and whether isolation is possible.
Priya: Initial mitigation: draining incoming traffic from pool-42 for tenant argos-prod and failing over to pool-43 (same region). Executing now.
Sam: Initiating traffic-split command:
```bash
rctl traffic-route set --tenant argos-prod --from pool-42 --to pool-43 --percent 100 --dry-run=false
```
Sam: Routing complete. Monitoring for error reduction.
incident-bot: mitigation-note: traffic routed to pool-43 (timestamp 2105000300). Alert suppressed for 10m while observing.
Priya: After failover, 5xx rate dropped to 2% within 90s. ArgosCorp still sees occasional timeouts while clients retry. Need deeper root cause for pool-42.
Elena: Pulling container logs from pool-42 node gpunode-17. Seeing frequent OOM-kill cycles on python-worker processes and repeated kernel-level GPU resets.
Sam: Hardware faults on gpunode-17 look likely. Marking node as unhealthy and launching replacement nodes. kube cordon/drain in progress.
Priya: For immediate customer comms, Jamal can you draft a short ack: what happened, impact, steps we took, and interim mitigation? Keep it non-technical.
Jamal: Drafting: "We're investigating an infrastructure instability affecting your dedicated inference pool in us-west-2. We failed over your traffic to a healthy pool; your requests should be restored. We'll follow up with an RCA and any credits."
Nikki: Sending that to ArgosCorp now. They asked whether this will affect SLA—what's our stance on credits? @Priya
Priya: We owe them a timeline + root cause. We'll propose a partial SLA credit pending RCA; hold off on formal offer until we confirm MTTR and recurrence probability.
Elena: For the RCA: initial hypothesis = GPU driver regression or thermal issue leading to kernel resets on gpunode-17 causing repeated worker restarts and cache eviction pressure. Collecting kernel logs, driver versions, and recent OS updates.
Sam: Also check autoscaler logs—did we hit scale limits? If dedicated pool hit capacity, retries might exacerbate failovers.
Priya: Action items: 1) Elena collect node logs & driver versions (due +2h). 2) Sam confirm autoscaler metrics & replacement node health (+1h). 3) Nikki confirm customer-facing note sent (+10m). 4) Jamal prepare exec summary and coordinate follow-up call (+30m). 5) Postmortem owner: Priya (RCA draft due EOD).
incident-bot: oncall-handoff: Priya -> Sam at 2105001200 (20m). Please acknowledge.
Sam: Acked, taking the handoff.
Jamal: ArgosCorp responded: "Thanks — please confirm any data exposure?" I told them there is no data exfiltration suspected; only service disruption.
Nikki: Keep them in status loop; offer optional follow-up call with our engineering lead after RCA.
Priya: Quick note for accounting: if RCA shows infrastructure hardware failure, credits per SLA clause 4.2 apply; we'll compute proportional credit for the impacted duration.
Elena: Found repeated kernel NVRM errors in dmesg and driver mismatches on gpunode-17. Snapshot attached to internal ticket. Also noticed GPU firmware versions on pool-42 nodes older than pool-43.
Sam: Replaced gpunode-17 and rebalanced pods. Pool-42 healthy now in staging, but recommending rolling upgrade of remaining nodes' drivers to match pool-43 to avoid recurrence.
Priya: Good. Let's not roll upgrades in prod without maintenance window. We'll plan a controlled driver rollout for the dedicated fleet.
Jamal: Drafting exec update: "We experienced an infrastructure failure impacting ArgosCorp's dedicated pool in us-west-2 for approx 14 minutes before failover; service restored with no suspected data loss. RCA forthcoming; action items include firmware/driver alignment and node replacement process improvements."
Nikki: Customer asked about timeline for RCA — they want it within 72 hours. Agreeable?
Priya: Yes, 72h is fine. RCA draft by EOD today, final within 72h. Also include proposed credit calculation.
Sam: For credit calc: impacted window 2105000120 -> 2105000240 (120s) per monitoring. I'll produce metrics and tokens affected (+3h).
Elena: Tagging eng-runtime to add a safeguard: automatic node driver version drift detection alert. I'll open a ticket.
incident-bot: incident-resolved: Status changed to mitigated at 2105000330. Root-cause-investigation in progress.
Priya: Closing loop: ensure post-incident comms: - public RCA to ArgosCorp - one-pager for execs - internal postmortem with timeline and blameless action items.
Jamal: I'll coordinate the external comms and cc legal for SLAs/credits language.
Nikki: I'll schedule a follow-up call with ArgosCorp Friday at 10am PT.
Priya: Thanks team. If anything new shows up, reopen this thread. :white_check_mark:
